PROPOSED DEFAULT, awaiting operator confirmation: the README is 470 KB (about 117000 tokens). Split it by Diataxis into a short README (under 300 lines) plus tutorial, how-to, reference and explanation pages, as ONE single-owner task with the README FROZEN for other agents while it runs (other tasks must wait or edit the new pages afterwards). The generated reference stays generated. SIZE L, RISK medium (large diff, link rot). FALSIFIER: README under 300 lines, doc links check passes, first run found in under 30 s. Reuse docs check. CONFORMANCE (r-everything-configurable, r-tell-dont-discover, r-no-shell, r-safe-by-default, r-docs-with-the-change, D-scope-focus-2026-11, R-audit-ux): every new limit, budget or default is a knob with a check; refusals name the next call in CLI and MCP form; nothing new is CLI-only unless person-only; new enforcement ships warn or off; docs change with the code.



STATE 2026-11-13 (queue fix-up): phase P-readme is done and the README is now 114111 B / 1648 lines (was 470 KB); the under-300-lines falsifier is still unmet, so this task stays open, narrowed to what P-readme did not do. Operator to confirm or close.

data.body:
Upgrade of UX-incremental-fold (link, do not duplicate; the operator decides which carries on). THIS DELETES NOTHING: the checkpoint is a derived, local, gitignored file like the snapshot; the full event log is never truncated, rewritten or moved; replay, export, verify and edit-by-correction work exactly as today and a full fold remains the reference (D-scale-answers 3, r-replay-compat, r-derive-dont-store). Design: State before localize/overlay, per-shard (size, prefix digest) marks and the adopted-event set; load checkpoint (0.47 s) plus mark (0.06 s) plus tail fold. A tail event that sorts before the checkpoint high key, or a newly adopted event, falls back to an older rung and then to a full fold. Key: explicit FOLD_REV, SCHEMA and FORMAT_LEVEL (not a source hash). Nothing is written below about 20k events. Kill switch DDFLOW_CHECKPOINT=0, deleting the file is the rollback; an older ddflow ignores an unknown-format file. ddflow upgrade --apply pre-warms it. REQUIRED TEST: an equivalence test, checkpoint plus tail equals a full fold byte for byte over a fixture corpus and the project's own log, including a late-sorting event from a merged clone. Rules r-derived-cache-bounded, r-upgrade-safe. SIZE L, RISK medium. FALSIFIER: show over 1.5 s idle at 132k, or State not byte-identical to a full fold. CONFORMANCE (r-upgrade-safe, r-replay-compat, r-derive-dont-store, r-derived-cache-bounded, r-bounded-everything, r-everything-configurable, r-no-shell, r-tell-dont-discover, r-unavailable-not-pass, r-docs-with-the-change, D-scale-answers, D-scope-focus-2026-11, R-scalability): the event log is never rewritten or truncated; every cache is derived, local and rebuildable; old logs replay identically; a new knob defaults to the old behaviour; an upgrade note ships with the change; a measurement that could not run is unavailable; a fix carries a regression test that fails against the unfixed code.



MEASURED 2026-11-13 (queue fix-up from the competition assessment, numbers re-checked on main): .ddflow/events 202 MB, about 195,800 event lines, 1665 shard files; the assessment measured ddflow next at 11.4 s CPU, ddflow status at 16.4 s CPU, growth about 4.8 MB/day (about 1.8 GB/year); the done B-gap-log-scale projected about 1 GB/year from 35 MB / 53k events on 2026-10-10, so its forecast is already wrong by about 2x. Priority P1.
